real my_prob;

//-------------------------------//

}"

stan_model="data {

int<lower=2> K;                       // num topics
int<lower=2> W;                       // num words
int<lower=1> M;                       // num docs

vector<lower=0>[K] alpha;             // hyperparameter of theta
vector<lower=0>[W] counts[M];         //gene counts
vector<lower=0>[W] phi_given[K];      //word in topic probability is normal log shaped

int<lower=1> batches[K];
int<lower=1> num_batches;

}

parameters {

simplex[K] theta[M];   // topic distribution for doc m 

#vector<lower=1, upper=100> [num_batches]  bias_magnitude;
real<lower=1, upper=100> bias_magnitude;
vector<lower=0> [W] perturbation;

} 

transformed parameters {
simplex[W] phi[K]; //simplex vlue of the linear equation across all genes 
vector[W] phi_hat_no_bias[K]; 

for(k in 1:K) phi_hat_no_bias[k] <- phi_given[k] .* perturbation;
for(k in 1:K) phi[k] <- softmax(phi_hat_no_bias[k]); 

}

model {
vector[K] log_phi[W]; 
vector[K] log_theta[M]; 
real my_prob;

for(m in 1:M) theta[m] ~ dirichlet(alpha);  // topic probability per document 
bias_magnitude ~ gamma(3, 0.5);
for(b in 1:num_batches) perturbation[b] ~ gamma(bias_magnitude, bias_magnitude-1);

//-------------------------------//
//   log transformation          //
//-------------------------------//

for(m in 1:M) log_theta[m] <- log(theta[m]); //just used to save computing
for(w in 1:W) for(k in 1:K) log_phi[w,k] <- log(phi[k,w]); //just used to save computing

//--------------------------------------------//
//        likelywood                          //
//--------------------------------------------//

for(m in 1:M) for(w in 1:W) if(counts[m,w]>0) {    
  my_prob <- log_sum_exp(log_theta[m] + log_phi[w]);
  increment_log_prob(my_prob * counts[m,w]);  
}

//-------------------------------//

}"


fit <-
  stan(
    model_code = stan_model,
    data = my.in,
    iter = 300
  )

We don't recommend the uniform(1, 100) priors because the
100 is artificial. Is it perhaps running up against a boundary
with 1 here in this?

real<lower=1, upper=100> bias_magnitude;
for(b in 1:num_batches) perturbation[b] ~ gamma(bias_magnitude, bias_magnitude-1);

For efficiency, you can vectorize the loop as

perturbation ~ gamma(bias, bias - 1);

But when you do this:

for(k in 1:K) phi_hat_no_bias[k] <- phi_given[k] .* perturbation;
for(k in 1:K) phi[k] <- softmax(phi_hat_no_bias[k]);

you have a problem in that perturbation isn't going to
be identified here. Given that phi_given is data (which I don't
understand, but that's another matter), you'll be able to induce
different scales in perturbation that lead to the same phi. You
really need to fix one of the dimensions, like setting one of the
phi_given to 0.

- Bob

parts:
I have to say THANKS for you suggestions Bob and all the community!

After your suggestion:

in b = simplex(a * x)         x ~ gamma(p, p-1) is not uniquely defined

I had few hard days to try 3 different alternatives to stabilize the model, than the simple and obvious solution came to me, and I want to share.

For making x with unique solution

we can do x ~ dirichlet([p_hat,p_hat,...p_hat])    in this case b = simplex(a * simplex()) works well.

I known probably is not the best explanation, but I'm open for any question :)

On Friday, April 29, 2016 at 3:04:09 PM UTC+10, Stefano wrote:
Thanks Bob,

as usual, you are right! BUT I want to add some more comments to see if this model can be still acceptable.

I reply in line.

On Friday, April 29, 2016 at 8:43:52 AM UTC+10, Bob Carpenter wrote:
We don't recommend the uniform(1, 100) priors because the
100 is artificial.  Is it perhaps running up against a boundary
with 1 here in this?  

- I added lower=1 because gamma can;t have the beta parameter (i.e., bias_magnitude-1) < 0.

- I added upper=100 because if there is no perturbation (perturbation = [1,1,....,1]), then bias_magnitude tends to Inf. I can leave withOUT upper, but then I should put a prior on bias_magnitude. What do you think?
 
  real<lower=1, upper=100> bias_magnitude;
  for(b in 1:num_batches) perturbation[b] ~ gamma(bias_magnitude, bias_magnitude-1);

For efficiency, you can vectorize the loop as

  perturbation ~ gamma(bias, bias - 1);


- Thanks. Also please not that perturbation is a matrix-like object
 
But when you do this:

  for(k in 1:K) phi_hat_no_bias[k] <- phi_given[k] .* perturbation;
  for(k in 1:K) phi[k] <- softmax(phi_hat_no_bias[k]);

you have a problem in that perturbation isn't going to
be identified here.  Given that phi_given is data (which I don't
understand, but that's another matter), you'll be able to induce
different scales in perturbation that lead to the same phi.  

- You are right! I haven't though about that.

indeed:

softmax( phi_hat[1, 2, 3]  .* perturbation[0.5, 1, 2])   ==    phi[ 0.059, 0.24, 0.71]
softmax( phi_hat[1, 2, 3]  .* perturbation[1, 2, 4])      ==    phi[ 0.059, 0.24, 0.71]

- BUT

Although I have infinite equally likely solutions, the prior on perturbation 

perturbation ~ gamma(bias_magnitude, bias_magnitude-1)  <<< mode of 1

Should ensure that among all possible solutions ([0.5, 1, 2] or [1, 2, 4])  it keeps the one closer to gamma with mode 1.

Am I thinking wrong?

 
You
really need to fix one of the dimensions, like setting one of the
phi_given to 0.

- Bob
